subject: Week 31: cruising begins - anchor every tall piece this weekend
bodyText:
This week
Cruising - sideways steps while holding furniture - is consolidating for early movers, though the CDC checkpoint remains 12 months; some infants also get themselves from prone to sitting now. Vocal turn-taking is increasingly conversational in rhythm, with mama and dada appearing inconsistently and no referent required yet. Imitation of simple actions - clapping, banging - is the week's cognitive headline.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Cruising falls with brief tears and normal behavior afterward - pad sharp coffee-table corners and let the curriculum run.
- [low concern] No first tooth yet - typical eruption spans 6-10 months, and later than that is usually unremarkable.
- [monitor] Persistent inability to bear weight on his legs, or no imitation of clapping or banging - add it to the 9-month-visit list.
- [call within 24h] Fever lasting more than 24 hours, or a new wheeze.
- [call now] After any fall: loss of consciousness, repeated vomiting, or unequal pupils - ER now. Bumps with normal behavior afterward need only observation.

Enrichment opportunities
- Anchor everything tall this weekend - TV, bookshelves, dressers, particle-board pieces especially: tip-over deaths in the crawling-to-climbing years are recurring and entirely preventable. AAP Childproofing Your Home: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/safety-prevention/at-home/Pages/Childproofing-Your-Home.aspx
- Play imitation games in rounds - clap, wave, bang, pause - and wait him out; imitation is how motor programs get acquired, and he will start serving first.
- Advance food textures from mashed toward chopped and soft finger foods, holding the top-9 allergen rotation at 2-3 exposures weekly each - texture progression by 9-12 months matters for oral-motor development. AAP Starting Solid Foods: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/feeding-nutrition/Pages/Starting-Solid-Foods.aspx
- Schedule a first structured playdate - 30 minutes of parallel play with one other baby is the right dose; parallel, not interactive, is the developmental mode at this age.

Upcoming
- Day 252-280 (Jan 18-Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit - if it is not on the calendar yet, book before holiday closures; the window includes influenza #2 and an iron rescreen.
- Day 222-228 (week of Dec 19, 2026): holiday week - brief visiting relatives on the 15-minute floor-level warm-up rule before anyone holds him.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Uses fingers to 'rake' food toward herself
  AAP window: day 210-270
  What to look for: Pre-pincer grasp. Coincides with starting finger foods.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/9-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/uses-fingers-rake/complete

- Crawls on hands and knees, or scoots
  AAP window: day 210-330
  What to look for: Some babies skip crawling and go straight to cruising — that is within normal range.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/crawls/complete

- Moves from sitting into a crawl or lie-down position
  AAP window: day 210-330
  What to look for: Postural transition. Predicts comfortable independent exploration.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/gets-from-sit-to-crawl/complete

- Cries or protests when a parent leaves the room
  AAP window: day 210-365
  What to look for: Peak separation anxiety. Healthy attachment, even when it makes drop-off hard.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/cries-when-parent-leaves/complete

- Catches himself with his arms when tipping over while sitting
  AAP window: day 210-300
  What to look for: Protective arm extension — reaching out to break a sideways or forward topple. Makes independent sitting safe enough for hands-busy play.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-8-to-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/catches-self-when-sitting/complete
